🎮 House Flipper — Not Recommend

⏱️ Hours Played: 1 hour
🎮 Platform: PC
📅 Played: 9/9/2026

⭐ Overall Thoughts

Low quality, overly priced, not well explained.

 ❤️ What I Liked

Mindless Grind: You can mindlessly grind away at this game, continual play, no pauses for story or anything like that. 
Worth Discounted Price: If you catch it when its $2.99 its worth it, otherwise I wouldn't bother.


 💀 What I Didn't Like

DLC: This game has ten DLC packs, they are also over priced for what you get and low quality. 
Graphics: The graphics are very low quality and the housing styles start to get repetitive. 

Mechanics: Aside from you having to mop the counters, tables, walls and ceiling not making any sense, the mechanics themselves are pretty bad and easily confusing. The game doesn't truly explain everything which also gets a bit annoying as you have to find easier ways to do things on your own. There is also no logic in terms of cleaning up the house and ensuring things are put back correctly. No repercussions to not doing it correctly.

Buggy: There are also jobs where you have to fix outlets that are hidden behind the clients counters, and when you move the counters you can't move them back to where they where so they are sticking out from the wall. 

Incomplete Tasks: Oh I hate games where you have to clean something like a window and you get 98% of the window clean and it just goes "Good Enough" And doesn't make or let you finish it so your OCD goes NUTS. HORRIBLY FRUSTRATING. 

 🎮 Gameplay

Repetitive, same houses, same jobs, over and over and over again for hours into the game. I played for an hour and I still haven’t gotten to do anything different aside from put in radiators, paint walls, and clean up trash and windows. 

 📖 Story / Characters

No story that I seen thank god. I wouldn’t have been able to get through an hour of slow game play plus that.


 🎨 Graphics / Atmosphere

Graphics are old school, they are not the worse I’ve seen but for a forty dollar …

claims.claim: Reviewers report that key bindings cannot be customized properly, citing restricted options and lack of left-handed friendliness.

citations.review_text: First of all, what the hell? Open the game and it's automatically advertising me things to buy right from the very start? Immediate turnoff! Try to configure key binds and half of them either won't bind to something or binding to other keys is forbidden. I wanted to like this game, but the short time I tried to play it, it wasn't any fun due to being forced to play a certain control scheme which is not left handed player friendly. The ad pitching on top of that to try get me to buy other things before I've even played was the nail in the coffin. I got the game to play the game not to be served ads within the game.
Can't rebind controls. I'd refund if I didn't get it for free. Missing basic accessibility features, should not be for sale.

single_points.text: One reviewer says there is lag, and using a controller helps the framerate and makes the experience more smooth compared to using an actual keyboard.

citation.review_text:
Okay, despite me giving this game a positive rating, I do need to preface by saying this game is NOT for everyone!!

Now originally, I intended on buying House Flipper 2, since I heard very good things about it. However, seeing that 39.99 price tag, I said "hell nah" and looked at the og instead. I felt that 24.99  was STILL a bit steep, given the games age, but I was too curious to turn away.

Now, after playing for a short while, I really do enjoy it. I've always loved older games (before you hate me, I know 2018 isn't THAT old, but compared to most sims nowadays? this is pretty much a relic in terms of graphics), and this one has an incredible charm to it. There's tons of tools that you use, each task feels simple yet unique, and the houses are honestly really fun to search through. That does not mean its without faults. The graphics are nothing spectacular, which is what I expected from the get-go. There is lag, especially if you use your actual keyboard to play (I found that using a controller actually helped the framerate and just overall made the experience more smooth). However, I did not find these issues to personally affect my enjoyment (I've emulated trashy PS1 and N64 games, so this is really nothing annoying for me).

Is it worth 25 bucks? That, reader, is for you to determine. If you like casual gameplay where you really don't have to think too hard + you like to decorate however you want + don't mind having mediocre framerate. Then yeah, maybe this is up your alley! 

Me, personally? I'm not too happy on the price tag. This game is pushing a decade old, it should honestly not be more than 15, especially given there is a remaster version out (also, why the hell is the remastered version so expensive??). Will I be refunding? No. I actually really enjoy the repetitive nature of this game, even if I do feel it was pricey for what its worth. 

Damn you Frozen Disrtict, you caught another helpless soul in your grasps!!

single_points.text: One reviewer says gameplay turns into a chore list when trying to meet buyer requirements because half the furniture items in each room category don't count toward changing the room type and there is no way to communicate that in game.

citation.review_text:
Close to a decade after release still plays like an unfinished mess.

If you are trying to actually meet the requirements of the different buyers instead of placing stuff to make it pretty, gameplay turns into a chore list. 

This is made EVEN WORSE by the fact that half the furniture items in each "room category" don't even count to change the room into the type you are looking for. There is no way to communicate that in game so you are stuck looking through ancient discussion hoping that some poor soul out there has been screwed over by the exact same piece of furniture as you.

There is no relevant progression system and gameplay turns stale really quick.

Overall, despite the massive popularity, it is by far the worst immersive sim I have played so far.

single_points.text: One reviewer says the base game is full of poor optimisation such as getting stuck on objects like the rims of staircases, items refusing to place due to invisible geometry and items not placing where the crosshair is aiming at random.

citation.review_text:
I'm someone who's played this game both on and off. Buying each bit of DLC that comes out up til the "remaster".
The game sucks.
The base game is still full of stupid glitches, bugs and poor optimisation such as getting stuck on objects like the rims of staircases, items refusing to place to due invisible geometry and items not placing where the crosshair is aiming at random. The base game is still ultra limiting as you cannot cut grass, have scant few options for external customisation despite being given access at the start of the game with the first office, seriously, if we aren't allowed to customise the outside properly in the base game, why even have it in the first place?
Next, you (Frozen District) CHARGE for the ability to cut grass and customise the outside in a meaningful way despite the game costing £21/$28/$39CAD already, you then charge an extra £13/$17/$24CAD???
Biblical levels of greed that i'd expect out of EA or Paradox.
But I'm far from done.
Next is the Cyberpunk DLC as a whole. Originally this DLC added like 60 items and a SINGLE NEW PLACE TO GO, and it remained that way for what? 2? 3 years? Before you decided to actually update it?
There is also the bugginess of the Pets DLC, the sheer unoptimised hell that was the Farm DLC, the unremarkability of the Dining DLC, and the utter disappointment that is the Apocalypse DLC still to this day.
And somehow, i'm STILL not done.
You then release the second game while the first is still a mess, which may i also add, is somehow JUST AS BUGGY. And even then, after that, you have to GALL to do a "remaster" that makes the game:
1) Run worse than it already did
2) Fuck up the aiming and placing system more than before
3) Charge EXTRA for shit
and on top of all that, then relase updates that apply to ONLY it?????????
And I haven't even hit on stuff like when you set out an ad looking for free QA testing instead of using an ACTUAL QA tester with all that money you fleece from people.

TL:DR:
Do…

single_points.text: One reviewer says there are announcements after booting up the game you can't disable before jumping into the title screen.

citation.review_text:
From my perspective, this game truly defines the power of creativity and endless possibilities throughout the availability of pre-loaded assets and custom assets. However, there are limitations that may inhibit actual creativity such as not placing the bed closely to the power outlet or the window locked in a reasonable position. (I understand this is an old game.)
Another example of what I don’t want to witness is the announcements after booting up the game you can’t disable before jumping into the title screen. I am not saying I loathed the game, I am just writing an honest review.

single_points.text: One reviewer says that when subscribed to workshop items, the game started crashing and running badly.

citation.review_text:
To be honest I have mixed feelings about the game. The game concept I truly love. I have bought almost all the DLCs. I really enjoy designing the houses to either sell or rent. I like what the DLCs add to the game. 

The issues I have is how the game runs. At one point, i subscribed to some workshop items. But the game started crashing and running badly. So I had to unsubscribe to ALL of them. There are only a handful I wanted. I just wanted a Jeep, Herbie the Lovebug, and a few items to make a recording studio in my "office". So I got rid of them, but the game still takes FOREVER to load. When I click continue game or go to any job or back to my office, it sometimes takes up to five minutes to even load. It also screen tears and lags. It does not matter how many items are in a house. I have watched my RAM to see if it spikes. The only time that seemed to be an issue was with the workshop items, ever since I got rid of those it never spikes up here, even when it glitches or lags. 

It honestly disappointing how bad the game is running. This is the only game I have these issues with. So, based on how fun the game is, I will recommend it, but I would also be weary about how the game may run. I'm still continuing to play, because I really enjoy it, I just wish it was running better.
